standard_prerequisites.name: A finitely generated projective module over a local ring is free, so the localizations of P at maximal ideals are free and the statement makes sense
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the rank and freeness language meaningful for the localizations appearing in the hypotheses.

standard_prerequisites.name: An element of a ring which is congruent to one modulo the Jacobson radical is a unit
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the congruence of the dual functional modulo the radical into a splitting over the whole ring.

standard_prerequisites.name: For a finite module over a Noetherian ring the first Tor group against a residue field is finite, and a finite dimensional vector space cannot surject onto a subquotient that has infinite dimension
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces an element t independent of the image of s + m in the fibre, which is the input to the next linear algebra step.

core_obligations: Reduce modulo the Jacobson radical: if in the quotient one can find m' in the image of M with the submodule generated by s' + m' a free direct summand, choose the splitting functional over the quotient, lift it to a functional on P by projectivity, choose m over m' and observe that the functional evaluated at s + m is congruent to one modulo the radical, hence a unit, so that the generated submodule is a free direct summand (proof lines 39036-39052).
Reduce further to the Noetherian case and set up the vanishing locus of the functionals phi_1, ..., phi_n evaluated at s + m inside the spectrum (proof lines 39054-39060).

Show that a vanishing locus containing a maximal ideal can always be made strictly smaller: the image of the intersection of M with the kernels of the phi_i in the fibre of P at that maximal ideal has infinite dimension, because the quotient of P by that intersection is a finite module and the kernel of the displayed map is a quotient of a finite Tor group, while the fibre itself is infinite dimensional; this yields an element t independent of the image of s + m and then a functional separating them (proof lines 39062-39090).

Iterate the strict decrease in the Noetherian topological space of the spectrum to reach a vanishing locus containing no closed point, hence empty, so that the functionals give a relation expressing one as a combination of the values of the chosen functionals at s + m (proof lines 39092-39100).

Read off that the composite of the map sending one to s + m followed by the combination of the functionals is the identity, which exhibits the submodule generated by s + m as a free direct summand of P (proof lines 39100-39104).
proof_roadmap: Work modulo the Jacobson radical first and lift a splitting from the quotient using projectivity and the unit criterion (proof lines 39036-39052).
In the Noetherian case, study the vanishing loci of finitely many functionals evaluated at a corrected element (proof lines 39054-39060).
Prove that any locus containing a closed point can be strictly decreased, using the infinite dimension of a suitable image in the fibre and the finiteness of a Tor group (proof lines 39062-39090).
Iterate until the locus is empty and translate the resulting relation into the splitting of the generated submodule (proof lines 39092-39104).
difficulty_reason: The statement produces, for a projective module with infinite rank localizations over a ring whose quotient by its Jacobson radical is Noetherian, an element m in a prescribed submodule M such that the submodule generated by s + m is a free direct summand, given that s and M already generate the whole module (statement lines 39025-39033). The proof has three stages: a reduction modulo the Jacobson radical where projectivity lifts the splitting and the unit criterion applies, a Noetherian stage where finitely many functionals define a vanishing locus, and an iteration argument in which any locus containing a closed point is strictly decreased because a suitable image in the fibre has infinite dimension while the relevant Tor group is finite (proof lines 39035-39104). The infinite dimension claim is the technical heart, since it is what supplies the element independent of the image of the corrected element.
